# Draft:First Byzantine expedition to Cilicia (1137-1138)

The Byzantine expedition to Cilicia between 1137 & 1138 was personally led by Emperor John II Komnenos of the Byzantine empire accompanied with his son (co-emperor) Alexios Komnenos launched a major military expedition to reassert its authority over Cilicia controlled by Armenian princes of the Rubenid dynasty which was also contested by the Principality of Antioch.
| commander1        = John II Komnenos   Alexios
| commander2        =  Leo I Thoros
}}
Background
following the Byzantine defeat at Manzikert in 1071. Ruben I led a successful Armenian revolt against the Byzantine Empire in the Taurus Mountains with the aid of the previous Byzantine commander Philaretos Brachamios who invited invited Armenian princes to settle in the Cilician and Taurus regions. establishing the independent Armenian Principality of Cilicia in 1080.
